findings_addressed.oracle: Direct inspection of async_bridge_mod._state.loop and _state.thread after shutdown (both must be None), then ensure_loop() must return a loop where is_running() is True — these are independent of the shutdown call itself and verify the actual side-effects of the production code path.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/ui/panels/async_bridge.py, comment out line 505 (_state.loop = None) inside shutdown_bridge_loop() — the assertion 'assert async_bridge_mod._state.loop is None' will fail because the stale stopped loop remains in _state.

notes: Removed the pre-existing autouse=True session fixture (_cleanup_bridge_loop) that violated RUF076 (pytest-fixture-autouse); the bridge thread is daemon=True so process exit handles teardown, and the hardened test itself exercises and verifies shutdown. Added ensure_loop() call before the first shutdown so state is guaranteed initialised, then asserted _state.loop is None and _state.thread is None after the first and second shutdown calls, and finally asserted recovered_loop.is_running() after calling ensure_loop() again to gate the full round-trip.
